title: Kitchen Cabinet Painting in Gainesville & Ocala, FL
description: Kitchen cabinet painting and refinishing in North Central Florida: degreasing, bonding primer, and a sprayed waterborne urethane enamel finish.
h1: Kitchen Cabinet Painting and Refinishing in North Central Florida
heroIntro: Give your kitchen a smooth, factory-style finish without tearing out the boxes. Doors are sprayed off site, frames are finished in place, and the coating is built to handle daily use.
card: Sprayed, factory-smooth cabinet finishes over a degreased, primed surface, without a full remodel.

secondary: refinish kitchen cabinets instead of replacing

sections.h2: When cabinet painting makes more sense than new cabinets
body: If your cabinet boxes are solid, the layout works, and the doors still close square, you probably do not need new cabinets. You need a new finish. Kitchen cabinet painting keeps the parts of your kitchen that work and replaces the part you are tired of looking at: honey oak, orange-toned maple, dated cherry, or a builder finish that has worn through at the handles.

Refinishing is not the right call for every kitchen. Swollen particleboard under the sink, delaminating thermofoil, or a layout you want to change are all signs that replacement is the better spend. We will tell you that on the walkthrough. Our article on whether to refinish or replace cabinets walks through the same checklist we use.

sections.h2: Why most DIY cabinet jobs peel, and what we do differently
body: Cabinets fail at the spots you touch every day: next to the range, under the sink, and around the pulls. The cause is almost always grease. Cooking oil works into the old finish, and any paint over it lets go right where your hand lands. If you are already living with that, our guide to a temporary fix for peeling cabinet paint can help until the job is done right.
Our prep is slow on purpose, because adhesion is everything on a cabinet.
bullets: Remove, label, and number every door, drawer front, and hinge
Degrease all surfaces with a dedicated cleaner, then rinse
Sand to a uniform dull so the primer can bite
Grain-fill open-grain oak where you want a smooth look
Apply a bonding primer suited to oak, maple, or other cabinet surfaces
Fill dings and seams, then sand the primer smooth before topcoat

sections.h2: The finish: waterborne urethane enamel, sprayed
body: Wall paint does not belong on cabinets. We use a waterborne urethane enamel from premium Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore lines, the same family of coating we use on doors and railings. It levels out smooth, cures hard, and cleans up without the yellowing you get from older oil-based enamels. The product is named on your estimate.

Doors and drawer fronts are sprayed flat in a controlled space and left to cure on racks before they come back. Cabinet boxes and face frames are sprayed in place, with the kitchen sealed off in plastic to keep overspray and dust contained. Two full coats is the baseline, with a third when we are going from a dark wood tone to a light color.

Oak is the most common cabinet we see in North Central Florida homes. If yours is oak, read how to paint oak cabinets to understand the choice between letting the grain show through and filling it for a smooth, modern look.

sections.h2: Hardware, glass doors, and small upgrades
body: A finish change is a good moment to rethink hardware. If you are switching from knobs to pulls, or to pulls of a different length, we fill the old holes before priming so they disappear under the new finish, then drill for the new hardware when the doors go back up. Glass-front doors are masked and finished on both sides, and open shelving inside cabinets can be painted to match or left natural.

Crown molding, light rail, and toe kicks are easy to overlook, but they frame the whole run of cabinets. They are included when listed on your estimate, and finished in the same enamel so the kitchen reads as one piece.

sections.h2: Timeline and living with the kitchen in progress
body: Most kitchens are out of service for about four to six working days. You can still use the fridge and, in most cases, the sink with a little planning; the stove area is the part that is tied up while boxes are being sprayed. Bathroom vanities, laundry cabinets, and built-in bookcases can be added to the same project and usually take less time.

When the doors go back up, hinges are adjusted so the gaps are even. You get labelled touch-up paint in the same color and sheen, plus a written workmanship warranty on top of the manufacturer's product warranty.

White and off-white are popular, but whites shift a lot under Florida light and next to granite or quartz. We can match a color from a sample door or a chip and bring a full-size drawdown, so you see the color next to your counters before we spray. If you want help with the whole kitchen palette, add a color consultation. Walls and trim in the same room can be scheduled through our interior painting service.
We refinish cabinets throughout the area; see local notes for Gainesville cabinet refinishing and Ocala cabinet refinishing.

faqs.q: How long is my kitchen out of service when cabinets are painted?
faqs.a: Most kitchens are out of service for about four to six working days. Doors are finished off site while the boxes are sprayed in place, and we plan the work so you keep access to the fridge.

faqs.q: Can you paint oak cabinets without the grain showing?
faqs.a: Yes. Oak has an open grain that shows through paint. We can grain-fill before priming so the doors read smooth, or skip that step if you like the texture. The choice is noted on the estimate.

faqs.q: Is painting cabinets cheaper than replacing them?
faqs.a: In most kitchens with sound boxes, refinishing costs much less than new cabinets and avoids countertop and plumbing work. We do not publish prices; the free estimate is based on the number of doors, drawers, and boxes and the condition of the existing finish.

faqs.q: What finish do you use on cabinets?
faqs.a: A waterborne urethane enamel from a premium Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore line, sprayed over a bonding primer. It cures hard and holds up to cleaning.

faqs.q: Can you paint bathroom vanities too?
faqs.a: Yes. Vanities, laundry cabinets, and built-ins get the same prep and finish and can be added to a kitchen project.
